title: Bridging hosted to dedicated: traffic smoothing, contractual patterns, and operational runway
content:
Context and objective
This is a working note for a customer POC where the ask is: start on hosted Redwood API for speed of delivery, then migrate to dedicated capacity when predictable throughput and data isolation are required. The goal of this doc is to capture pragmatic bridge patterns, suggested contract language/SLAs, traffic smoothing tactics, and an operational runway (runbook + rollback conditions) so solutions + customer can agree on low-risk migration steps.

Audience
- Solutions engineering (primary)
- Customer SRE/platform leads (secondary)
- Account team and legal for contract snippets

High-level constraints observed in this POC
- Customer has bursty daily traffic with peak factor ~12x baseline.
- Initial MVP requires sub-150ms P95 latency for short-chat workloads; long-form generation not in scope for phase 1.
- Data classification: PII in request metadata but not persisted to model; customer requires VPC peering for Dedicated.
- Budget: soft limit for first 90 days; must show unit-cost delta hosted → dedicated by week 6.

Recommended bridge patterns (ordered by risk/complexity)
1) Dual-routing with gradual weight shift (preferred)
   - Start 100% hosted. Create a Dedicated pool provisioned at ~20–30% of expected sustained baseline.
   - Route a small % of production traffic (1–5%) to Dedicated using header-based traffic-weights. Observe latency, errors, and cost.
   - Increase weight weekly (5–10pp) while monitoring QoS and cache hit behavior.
   - Benefit: smallest blast radius; operationally simple routing change; allows model variant testing on Dedicated.

2) Canary-by-route (fine-grain)
   - For multi-route APIs (chat, embeddings, rerank), canary only high-value routes to Dedicated first.
   - Useful when customers want isolation for specific datasets or when Dedicated capacity is constrained.

3) Burst-offload with prefix caching (cost-first)
   - Keep baseline traffic on Dedicated and configure Hosted as overflow for large bursts. Implement token-aware prefix caching on Dedicated to maximize reuse; route overflow using queue depth or latency-based circuit breakers.
   - Benefit: deterministic cost for baseline, hosted used only for spikes. Complexity increases due to circuit-breaker tuning.

Traffic smoothing and operational knobs
- Initial capacity sizing: base Dedicated to 1.2x the observed 95th percentile of baseline (exclude known big spikes).
- Autoscale policy: prefer fast scale-up (short cooldown ~30s) + conservative scale-down (5–10m) to avoid thrashing.
- Request shaping: apply soft QPS caps at the ingress to avoid saturating Dedicated until cache warm-up finishes.
- Rate fencing: map customer API keys to dedicated tenant IDs so routing control is key-specific.
- Backpressure signals: enforce 429/503 handling strategy in client SDKs and provide token bucket guidance in integration notes.

Cost and contract patterns to propose early
- Minimum-commit runway: propose 3-month commit with a break clause at month 2 if P95 latency or cost-per-1k tokens exceed agreed thresholds.
- Billing split: host baseline as committed monthly reservation for Dedicated; report delta usage on Hosted as overage at standard rates.
- SLAs during bridge: agree on latency bands for both Hosted and Dedicated for the trial window. Example: Hosted best-effort, Dedicated P95 under 200ms during business hours.
- Data handling addendum: include VPC peering timeline and a clear acceptance test for private networking before cutting heavier weights to Dedicated.

Operational runway (checklist + runbook steps)
Pre-migration (week -2 to 0)
- Baseline telemetry collection: 2 weeks of production traces (latency distribution, seq length, token mix). Pin representative prompt set.
- Cost model: run token-level cost sim for expected shape and document expected monthly delta.
- Provision Dedicated pool: initial instance types and rough autoscale thresholds.
- Acceptance tests: latency, tail, and correctness on a canned prompt set; snapshot baseline metrics.

Migration phase (week 0–6)
- Day 0: route 1% traffic to Dedicated; run acceptance test every 4 hours.
- Week 1–3: expand weight to 10–30% depending on error/latency. Keep an eye on cache-warm metrics; expect initial increase in tokens served until KV caches populate.
- Week 3–6: shift to 60–90% if metrics stable. Run a cost review at week 6 to decide on commit.

Rollback criteria (explicit triggers)
- Sustained P95 latency increase > 30% on Dedicated for 30+ minutes.
- Error rate on Dedicated > 0.5% or surpasses Hosted by >0.3pp for 15+ minutes.
- Cost-per-1k tokens on Dedicated > projected committed rate by 25% for 48 hours.

Post-cutover (stabilization)
- Observe 2–4 week stabilization window. Document cache hit rates, model latency variance, and any error patterns tied to autoscaling.
- Optional: right-size instance types and adjust autoscale granularity after 2 weeks of steady-state.

Integration and testing notes
- Model variants: pin model versions by route to avoid semantic drift between Hosted and Dedicated. If unavoidable, run A/B evals with a labeled prompt set.
- Observability: enable token-level tracing, per-request route tags, and distributed tracing to identify cross-hosted/dedicated anomalies.
- Load testing: synthetic load should mirror token distribution (not just RPS) to surface KV cache behavior and kernel selection differences.

Security and compliance items
- VPC peering checklist: IP allowlists, TLS termination points, route table verification, and test webhook endpoints in staging.
- KMS: Dedicated must have customer-managed keys if requested; include rotation cadence and validation steps.
- Audit logs: ensure request/response metadata required for compliance is captured on both planes. Provide sample retention config.

Open questions and TODOs (working list)
- How to quantify cache warm-up cost exactly for pricing conversations? (Priya to run 3 synthetic permutations by 2025-11-14)
- Customer legal feedback needed on the 3-month break clause; draft suggested language for account team.
- Confirm target Dedicated instance families with infra (Ethan) and expected lead time for provisioning.

Quick links and references
- Confluence: bridging patterns (linked above)
- JIRA: JIRA-1124 (customer POC ticket)
- Simulation repo: git://repo/internal/poc-traffic-simulations#42

Notes to self
- Keep the first dedicated pool intentionally small to preserve negotiating leverage on commit.
- Avoid converting all routes at once unless customer explicitly wants a big-bang migration and accepts higher risk.

Appendix: suggested lightweight contract snippet (for AE/legal review)
- "Customer may provision a Dedicated pool subject to an initial 3-month commitment. Either party may terminate this commitment at the end of month 2 if agreed SLA and cost thresholds in Appendix A are not met. During the trial period, Redwood will provide reasonable assistance to migrate traffic patterns and will allow rollback to Hosted with no penalty."

End of working note. Feedback appreciated — will iterate after Priya's cache-warm simulations and Ethan's infra sizing confirmation.
